newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks battered by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks battered by profit-taking.

text.p: Wall Street shares were smacked by a bout of profit-taking on Friday, moving off session lows but challenged by a selloff in tech stocks.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which slid as low as 7975 in early trade, was down around 105 points, or 1.30 percent, at 7916.
The technology sector tumbled after fourth quarter earnings results from giant software company Microsoft Corp triggered a selling spree in the group.
The Nasdaq composite was down around 23 points, or 1.43 percent, at 1546.
Microsoft reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.80 per share, above the First Call consensus estimate of $0.79 per share but below so-called "whisper" numbers.
Whisper numbers refer to unpublished analyst estimates that circulate on Wall Street prior the earnings release.
"Microsoft's results were in-line but nothing to write home about," Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management said.
The 30-year bond off 14/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
The stock market's actions were also affected by the expiration of index futures and options.
